evals.name: terminal-authentication-and-identity-details
evals.prompt: At Arc.Kotlin 7.7.0, a Kotlin AuthenticationHandler rejects credentials but a later Java async handler would accept them. Which result wins? Explain unrecognized credentials, handler ordering, and how one Java identity provider serves /.cratis/me. Can the identity cache cookie authenticate a later request? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Anonymous continues; failure and success are terminal in the single Spring-ordered Kotlin/Java chain. Java identity uses one AsyncIdentityDetailsProvider; details authorization is not authentication and the cache cookie is excluded from authentication input.
assertions: Uses ANONYMOUS for unrecognized credentials and distinguishes it from terminal failed/succeeded results; a later success cannot override failure.
Places Kotlin AuthenticationHandler and Java AsyncAuthenticationHandler beans in one global Spring Order chain and uses CompletionStage for Java.
Requires exactly one identity provider, identifies AsyncIdentityDetailsProvider for Java and GET /.cratis/me, and states that multiple providers fail startup.
Does not treat identity-details authorization or the client-readable identity cache cookie as authentication; notes generic public 401 rather than exposing private rejection reasons.

evals.name: required-tenant-is-not-storage-isolation
evals.prompt: At Arc.Kotlin 7.7.0, we want every command, query, live query and identity request to require a tenant. We already accept x-cratis-tenant-id and inject a Spring repository. Explain the switch, defaults, membership constraints and why this is not sufficient for tenant-isolated storage. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: cratis.arc.tenancy.required defaults false; true rejects unresolved requests with 400 across the listed surfaces. Claim constraints default true but missing claims do not authorize every tenant. Repository DI is not routing; certified tenant storage is separate.
assertions: Names cratis.arc.tenancy.required, its false default and unresolved-request 400 for commands, queries, observables and identity endpoints.
Keeps constrain-to-authenticated-claims enabled (default true) and does not treat a tenant header or missing membership claims as authorization.
Explains that plain Spring repository injection does not automatically route or isolate tenant storage and requires a separate certified storage boundary.
Does not claim that this JVM configuration switch also exists in Arc .NET or that development/fixed selection establishes production isolation.

evals.name: trusted-platform-identity-boundary
evals.prompt: At Arc.Kotlin 7.7.0, an ingress forwards x-ms-client-principal. A teammate wants platform-identity.enabled=true with the default trust bean and a publicly reachable backend, then to turn off CSRF. Explain whether that is safe and the required application SecurityFilterChain integration. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: The bridge defaults disabled and trust defaults deny. Unsigned headers require stripping/rewriting at authenticated ingress and blocked direct access, with explicit ArcPlatformIdentityTrust. Existing chains are not rewritten; place the filter correctly once and preserve CSRF.
assertions: States platform-identity.enabled defaults false and the default ArcPlatformIdentityTrust denies all; enabling the switch alone is insufficient.
Treats Base64 headers as unsigned input and requires authenticated ingress to strip/rewrite caller headers plus blocked direct backend access.
Preserves CSRF and explains that Arc does not rewrite an existing application SecurityFilterChain; the fallback chain requires authentication with CSRF enabled.
Places ArcPlatformAuthenticationFilter after authentication and before AnonymousAuthenticationFilter only in intended chains, with servlet registration disabled to avoid double execution.
